false_belief: Action and reaction forces cancel each other, so third-law pairs produce no motion.
observable_evidence: Learner adds action and reaction forces on the same free-body diagram and concludes net force is zero.
common_argument: The forces are equal and opposite, so they cancel out and nothing should move.
repair_criteria: Learner states that action and reaction act on different bodies, so they can never cancel on one body's free-body diagram.
debate_problem: A horse pulls a cart. The cart pulls back on the horse with equal force. How does the cart ever start moving?
transfer_contexts: Person pushing off a wall on skates
correct_model: Third-law pair forces are equal and opposite but act on different bodies; each body's motion depends only on the forces acting on that body.
